scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

P-M2C.name: meter-to-cash
steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

DA-MDMS.name: MDMS AMI read event log (system of record for AMI reads)

DA-RULES.name: billing import validation rule change log

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

H-REQUESTER-FR.statement: Dispute surge due to incorrect bills causing customer complaints.

H-AMI-READ-ISSUE.statement: Delayed or missing AMI reads lead to estimation errors and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-GAP.statement: Contractor field reads are incomplete or delayed, causing estimation substitution.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: Recent changes to billing import validation rules introduced systematic billing errors.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field manual read completion for Aug‑Sep 2026 is 88%, below the 95% target, indicating a gap in field reads that could drive estimation substitution and wrong bills.
The tariff change log contains no entries, indicating that no tariff changes were recorded in the billing system during the observed period, thus tariff changes are not a source of the wrong bills.

The observation shows more disputed bills from actual reads (1785) than from estimated reads (1240), indicating that wrong bills are not solely due to estimation errors and suggesting other causes affect both read types.

E-04.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The field operations manager reports a shortage of three meter readers since July, causing routes to run late and resulting in estimated bills for those customers.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder states there has been no tariff change this year, indicating tariff revisions are not driving the recent wrong bills.

Dispute ticket volume rose from about 600 per month in June‑July to over 1,100 in August and 1,260 in September, showing a clear surge starting in August that matches the stakeholder claim of doubled dispute tickets since August.

Dispute response times are within the SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs SLA 3 days), indicating that the surge in dispute volume is not driven by slow responses. This suggests the underlying cause of wrong bills lies elsewhere, such as read or billing issues.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract allows the utility to request route priority changes, but any such change must be confirmed by the Field Operations Manager. This indicates a controlled process for adjusting field dispatch that could be used to improve manual read completion.

problem_definition.root_problem: Low field manual read completion below the 95% target increases estimation substitution, which leads to higher billing dispute tickets.

trace.summary: Low field manual read completion below the 95% target increases estimation substitution, which leads to higher billing dispute tickets.

While structural remedies are pursued, completion may not reach target quickly enough to halt dispute growth; an agent could provide interim dispute‑ticket responses and bill‑adjustment guidance until structural changes take effect.

structural_remedies.description: Increase field reader headcount by three (hire/train contractors) to meet the 95% completion target, addressing the reader shortage noted by SH-FIELD (E-04).
structural_remedies.rationale: Hiring and onboarding cannot be completed within the remaining ~225 minutes.; residual gap: If headcount is not increased promptly, completion remains at 88% (E-01), leaving estimation substitution and dispute volume unresolved.

structural_remedies.description: Use the field dispatch contract to request route priority changes, obtaining runtime confirmation from the Field Operations Manager as required by K-DISPATCH and E-08, to prioritize late routes and improve completion.
structural_remedies.rationale: A request can be made immediately; the contract already allows such changes with manager confirmation.; residual gap: Effectiveness depends on manager approval and actual impact on completion; may not reach the 95% target, leaving a partial gap.

structural_remedies.description: Repair the degraded MDMS export tool (currently DEGRADED per runtime tool_health) to ensure AMI reads are available, reducing reliance on manual reads.
structural_remedies.rationale: Vendor‑provisioned access restoration may exceed the remaining time window.; residual gap: Does not directly raise manual read completion; estimation substitution will persist for accounts lacking AMI reads (E-01).

solution_design.why_agent: While structural remedies are pursued, completion may not reach target quickly enough to halt dispute growth; an agent could provide interim dispute‑ticket responses and bill‑adjustment guidance until structural changes take effect.
solution_design.bridge_sunset_condition: Field manual read completion meets or exceeds 95% target (E-01 becomes true) or dispute volume per month returns to ≤650 (SC-S-01 met)
unfinished_scope: Increase field reader headcount by three (hire/train contractors) to meet the 95% completion target, addressing the reader shortage noted by SH-FIELD (E-04).
